newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's ADIG says dollar's rise not over yet.
newsitem.headline: Germany's ADIG says dollar's rise not over yet.

text.p: Germany's ADIG Allgemeine Deutsche Investment GmbH fund management company is betting on a stronger dollar and thus a further boost for European export shares, managing director Christian Humbert said.

"The end of the road has not been reached at 1.69 (marks to the dollar)," Humbert told reporters late Monday evening, after a day which saw the dollar pop briefly above the 1.70-mark level. The dollar was above 1.70 marks Tuesday morning.
Humbert declined to give a precise forecast for the point at which the dollar's advance would end.
"It would not make sense to say five pfennigs from here or ten pfennigs. At the end of the day we are clearly of the opinion that the dollar is rising," he said.

Jointly owned by Commerzbank AG and Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, ADIG has some 46 billion marks under management, of which 28 billion is invested in bonds, nine billion in equities and nine billion in the money market.
In equities, ADIG is betting on European markets, citing the region's moderate growth rates, weak wage pressures and low interest rates.
While generally positive on Germany, and predicting a level of 2,400 to 3,500 points for the DAX this year, ADIG believes the market has rushed ahead too quickly so far this year.
"The market is clearly overbought," said ADIG senior stock fund manager Kerstan von Schlotheim.
In Germany, ADIG sees the steel, engineering and car sectors as most promising.
The company is however underweight in retail shares because of weak home consumption, cautious on utilities, including telecommunications and neutral on the banking sector.
